clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her late 30s presented to the outpatient department with a 6-month history of progressive bilateral vision loss, with the right eye more severely affected than the left. On initial ophthalmic examination, fundoscopy revealed optic nerve head hemangioblastomas with papilloedema in both eyes, a peripheral retinal hemangioblastoma in the left eye (inferotemporal to disc), and an epiretinal membrane with pseudohole in the right eye. The patient had a significant prior history of brain surgery 7 years earlier for cyst resection, and a family history of similar vision complaints in her deceased brother (who died in his late 20s, 4 years prior). When the patient returned after several months without seeking initial treatment, her vision had deteriorated markedly to light perception with accurate projection of rays in the right eye and finger count close to face in the left eye. MRI of the head documented multiple cystic space-occupying lesions in the posterior fossa and a well-circumscribed mass on the right optic nerve in the optic canal. Systemic imaging revealed bilateral enlarged kidneys with variable-sized cortical cysts and a soft tissue lesion in the left kidney, as well as an extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma in the right paramedian retroperitoneum at the L5 level. These multisystem findings—ocular hemangioblastomas, CNS hemangioblastomas/cysts, renal cysts with a renal lesion, and extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma—are pathognomonic for Von Hippel-Lindau disease.
